files_reviewed: db/schema.rb (users + organizations table sections + version line)
notes:
Traced all four assigned files against the feature delta (git diff 62dd55867..fc3f047f9) and the spec (§3, §4.5, §8). No defects found; everything is internally consistent.

omniauth.rb: the ONLY feature change is line 14, allowed_keys extended from %w[partner referral] to %w[partner referral utm_source utm_campaign utm_data internal_ref]. The pre-existing capture loop (line 17-20: value = rack_request.params[key]; tracking_params[key] = value if value && !value.empty?) handles all four new keys correctly. Verified utm_data nested-hash capture (dispatch-required): the SSO form posts utm_data[<inner_key>] hidden inputs which Rack parses into a Hash at rack_request.params['utm_data']; Hash is truthy and responds to empty?, so a populated hash is captured and an empty {} is correctly skipped; it rides env['rack.session'][:oauth_tracking] and, with the :json cookie serializer (cookies_serializer.rb), round-trips with string keys to merged_tracking['utm_data'] in the callback. utm_source/utm_campaign/internal_ref arrive as strings and use String#empty?. The `if tracking_params.any?` session guard and the Rails.logger.info line are pre-existing and unchanged. M1 (untyped/uncapped server-side ride, crafted-POST cookie overflow) is the settled ruling and NOT re-flagged; crafted non-string values (e.g. utm_source[]= producing an Array, or utm_data=foo producing a String cast into the jsonb column later) fall inside M1's accepted no-server-side-sanitization design. Observation only (not flagged): the pre-existing Rails.logger.info now also logs marketing attribution values; benign, pre-existing logging line, low-sensitivity data.

Migrations: both are new files, class name matches camelized filename (AddAttributionColumnsToUsers / AddAttributionColumnsToOrganizations), both inherit ActiveRecord::Migration[6.1] (matches analog 20260622182504). Both use add_column inside `change`, which is auto-reversible. Column types are exactly string/string/jsonb/string. NO null: false and NO defaults on any column — matches spec §3 / D6 (absent stays nil, not {}), and structurally mirrors the analog (add_column with no null constraint on nullable columns). Nullable no-default add_column on the large users/organizations tables is a metadata-only Postgres operation, no table rewrite / lock concern. Timestamps 20260715233505 (users, first per spec ordering) then 20260715233506 (organizations) are sequential and are the two newest files in db/migrate (verified: next-newest is 20260622204646). Org migration running after users migration has no runtime dependency (org copies from current_user; both applied pre-deploy).

schema.rb: version bumped from 2026_06_11_120003 to 2026_07_15_233506, which exactly equals the latest migration file 20260715233506 — no schema/migration version mismatch. Both tables carry all four columns with correct types: organizations lines 1089-1092 (utm_source string, utm_campaign string, utm_data jsonb, internal_ref string) confirmed inside create_table "organizations" (1033-1093); users lines 1285-1288 (same four, same types) confirmed inside create_table "users" (starts 1248), placed before the table's indexes. No default/null attributes on the new columns, correctly contrasting the adjacent `settings` jsonb (default: {}, null: false on both tables) — the deliberate D6 distinction is faithfully reflected. Verified the intermediate migrations 20260622182504/20260622204646 and the base's 2026_06_11_120003 version line are a PRE-EXISTING anomaly on the jobs/ai_job_criteria tables (base schema already contained ai_job_application_summaries_count while its version line lagged); those tables are outside my assigned scope and the version bump here is the correct max-migration value, not a mismatch introduced by this feature.
